questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most crucial aspects were my love for French culture, especially literature, film, café culture, manner of life, and their worldview. The French love beauty and have a very different approach to life then my countrymen of my native Denmark, an attitude which I found appealing. Furthermore, I wanted to make sure that I had a decent level of competence in spoken French when finishing my bachelor in French culture and language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. As long as I knew the basics of asking questions, such as directions, I encountered no significant problems. The team at UCPHabroad were also a great help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None in particular that I recall, but it was relatively easy to find my university, classes, and such, since I had received a fair amount of instructions before arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult to say, since I found it via a friend of my father's.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rather expensive in Paris proper, that's for sure.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to register at a certain office, have my date of arrival at the institution signed, and sign up for a student card. Fairly easy, simply had to meet up at the time and location which was described in the documents I received.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Most likely, but since none was necessary I did not check.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very much so; it was a bit difficult to understand the way to do it, but the faculty was always very helpful and patient.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the documents you receive carefully some time before the date of registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some were more difficult than others; I mostly took first and third year classes. The ones that were too difficult I changed and there was a great deal of leeway, since one could change classes until the Easter vacation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less focused on dialogue, more on listening to lecturs and writing notes, sometimes verbatim. I prefered it frankly.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.answer:
L4LIZ20A - Littérature et culture
L6LIZ071 - Patrimoine culturel français (option FLE)
L6LI99AN - ANGLAIS POUR LM: LANGUE ET LITTERATURE (niveau B2 et plus)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depending on your level of French mostly first and second year classes. There are also options to take classes in English which I would recommend, simply to not stress out too much about the language barrier, and to give the mind a break.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Various, but I did not pay them any mind.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Frequent walks through Paris and reading the newspaper for French practice at cafés.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Besides the basic tourist traps? The cathedrals of Chartres, Amiens, and Reims.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took me some months before I recovered from the slight culture shock, but I came to feel home at ease in Paris after about 2-3 months.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not many, most French seem a bit more isolated than expected. They are however kind and friendly, so I would not worry about talking to them - it's the befriending aspect that is a bit more difficult, getting them to really open up.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The French sense of humor is rather different from Danish and a Anglo-American humor. It's something that's difficult to really explain, but there is a definite difference which can be difficult to understand at first.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Just about everything! Contrary to what I have been told, the French are some of the most polite people I have ever meet. Perhaps not the always the warmest, I appreciated the norms of greeting before and after leaving a store or place, even if you're strangers. Besides that, the ease of enjoyment, simple pleasures such as taking a walk, sitting down around Paris or in a café, the food and bakeries, the weather in the warmer months, hearing the language on the streets, and so on.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Master the basics of greeting when entering a store or place and saying goodbye - politeness is vital for good interaction with most French people. 
Learn how to relax and enjoy the city, not to necessarily go to Versailles or Louvre all the time, but to just take a walk throughout the city. I do not think there is a city I have just spontaneously explored than Paris. 
Visit and buy from actual shops that sell meat, fish, cheese, bakeries, and please do not just buy everything at a supermarket.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep calm and accept that there is a lot of bureaucracy and be ready to ask questions if you have the slightest doubt whether via mail or in person.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The totality of French culture. It's really wonderful if you try not to force it into a box of romanticised expectations.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely the language: I feel that there are sadly many things I have missed because I have not mastered the language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
